questions.question: Which of the following is widely accepted as a core principle demonstrating why democracy is superior to non-democratic regimes?
options: It eliminates the need for national defense spending completely
It guarantees uniform wealth distribution within two fiscal quarters
It allows executive heads to rule without any parliamentary consultation
It promotes equality among citizens and enhances the dignity of the individual
questions.explanation: Democracy is considered a better form of government because it promotes equality among citizens, enhances individual dignity, improves decision quality, provides conflict resolution mechanisms, and allows room to correct mistakes.

questions.question: In a democratic government, to whom are elected rulers fundamentally accountable?
options: Only to the international monetary institutions
To the citizens and electorate who vote them into power
To hereditary feudal landholders
To supreme military commanders
questions.explanation: In a democracy, we are most concerned with ensuring that people will have the right to choose their rulers and people will have control over the rulers. Whenever possible, citizens should participate in decision-making.

questions.question: Why do democratic decision-making processes often take more time compared to non-democratic dictatorships?
options: Because democratic legislatures only meet once every ten years
Because computers and telecommunications are legally banned in parliament
Because democracies follow established norms, deliberation, and extensive consultation before arriving at a decision
Because judges must personally approve every municipal bylaw
questions.explanation: Democracy is based on the idea of deliberation and negotiation. A non-democratic government can take decisions very quickly because it does not have to bother about consultation or parliamentary majorities. But democracy follows norms and procedures, resulting in more acceptable decisions.

questions.question: The right and the means available to a citizen in a democracy to examine the process of government decision-making is termed:
options: Transparency
Autocracy
Bureaucratic hegemony
Judicial oligarchy
questions.explanation: A citizen who wants to know if a decision was taken through the correct procedures can find this out. She has the right and the means to examine the process of decision making. This is known as transparency.

questions.question: In India, which landmark legislation enacted in 2005 empowered citizens to inspect government records and uphold transparency?
options: National Education Policy Act
Consumer Protection Act
Right to Information Act (RTI Act 2005)
Industrial Disputes Act
questions.explanation: The Right to Information (RTI) Act of 2005 empowers Indian citizens to seek information from public authorities, promoting transparency and holding the government accountable.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Civics, Chapter 5, Box Note on Transparency

questions.question: Why is a democratic government regarded as a 'legitimate government' despite occasional inefficiency or slowness?
options: Because it is the people's own freely elected government
Because it is chosen by international observers and foreign treaties
Because it commands a standing army larger than its civil workforce
Because it suppresses dissenting political opinions entirely
questions.explanation: A democratic government may be slow, less efficient, not always very responsive or clean. But a democratic government is the people's own government. That is why there is an overwhelming support for the idea of democracy all over the world.

questions.question: When comparing economic growth records between democracies and dictatorships during the period 1950–2000, evidence shows that:
options: Democracies grew at ten times the speed of any authoritarian state
Economic growth was completely zero across all democratic nations
No measurable economic data was recorded during this 50-year period
Dictatorships had a slightly higher rate of economic growth overall
questions.explanation: If you consider all democracies and all dictatorships for the fifty years between 1950 and 2000, dictatorships have slightly higher rates of economic growth. However, among poor countries, the difference in economic growth is negligible.

questions.question: Economic development of a nation depends on several factors besides the form of government. Which of the following is NOT a primary determinant?
options: Country's population size and demographic profile
The ruling dynasty's astrological horoscope
Global economic situation and foreign trade partnerships
Cooperation from other nations and economic priorities adopted
questions.explanation: Economic development depends on several factors: country's population size, global situation, cooperation from other countries, economic priorities adopted by the country, etc. Astrological beliefs have no factual role.

questions.question: Democracies are based on political equality, yet in the economic sphere they have frequently struggled to:
options: Hold universal adult franchise general elections
Allow legal registration of opposition political parties
Permit citizens to criticize parliamentary policies
Reduce growing income inequalities between the ultra-rich and the impoverished
questions.explanation: Parallel to the process of bringing individuals into the political arena on an equal footing, we find growing economic inequalities. A small number of ultra-rich enjoy a highly disproportionate share of wealth and incomes, while the poor struggle for basic needs.

questions.question: In countries like Bangladesh, what stark economic reality coexists with political democracy?
options: All citizens belong to the top 1% global income tier
Private commerce and agricultural markets are legally outlawed
More than half of its total population lives in acute poverty
The national poverty rate reached zero in 1995
questions.explanation: In actual life, democracies do not appear to be very successful in reducing economic inequalities. In Bangladesh, more than half of its population lives in poverty. People in several poor countries are now dependent on the rich countries even for food supplies.

questions.question: What is the primary mechanism through which democracies handle social differences and ethnic conflicts?
options: By evolving open mechanisms and constitutional dialogue to negotiate and accommodate differences peacefully
By permanently disenfranchising minority cultural groups
By declaring martial law whenever community disagreements arise
By expelling linguistic minorities to neighbouring countries
questions.explanation: No society can fully and permanently resolve conflicts among different groups. But we can certainly learn to respect these differences and we can also evolve mechanisms to negotiate the differences. Democracy is best suited to produce this outcome.

questions.question: In order to successfully accommodate social diversity, democracy must fulfill two conditions. The first condition is that:
options: The minority community must be stripped of judicial rights
The majority must always work with the minority so that governments represent the general collective view
Elections must be won exclusively on religious identity appeals
The opposition leader must be exiled during legislative voting
questions.explanation: Condition 1: It is necessary to understand that democracy is not simply rule by majority opinion. The majority always needs to work with the minority so that governments function to represent the general view.

questions.question: What is the second essential condition for a healthy democracy regarding majority rule?
options: The majority must seize all private commercial banks
The majority must suspend the constitution every alternate year
The majority party must permanently abolish local municipal elections
Rule by majority must not become rule by a single religious, racial, or linguistic majority community permanently
questions.explanation: Condition 2: Rule by majority must not become rule by majority community in terms of religion or race or linguistic group. Rule by majority means that in case of every decision or election, different persons and groups may and can form a majority.

questions.question: How has democracy strengthened the long struggle of women for equality and respect in patriarchal societies?
options: By completely eliminating domestic chauvinism overnight
By replacing all male judges with royal appointees
By providing a moral and legal recognition to the principle of gender equality, making discrimination legally challengeable
By creating a single-party female dictatorship
questions.explanation: Most societies across the world were historically male dominated. Long struggles by women have created some sensitivity today that respect to and equal treatment of women are necessary ingredients of a democratic society. Once the principle is recognised, it becomes easier for women to wage a struggle.

questions.question: How has democracy in India impacted historically disadvantaged and discriminated castes?
options: It has made traditional caste discrimination legally mandatory
It has strengthened their claims for equal status and equal opportunities through constitutional guarantees and voting power
It has forced all backward communities to abandon agriculture
It has eliminated all reservations in public employment and education
questions.explanation: Democracy in India has strengthened the claims of the disadvantaged and discriminated castes for equal status and equal opportunities. There are still instances of caste-based inequalities and atrocities, but these lack moral and legal foundations.

questions.question: What is meant by the statement: 'The most distinctive thing about democracy is that its examination never gets over'?
options: As democracy passes one test, people produce another test; people constantly demand more benefits and better governance
School examinations are conducted every weekend under democratic law
Civil servants must take competitive exams every calendar month
Democratic parliaments dissolve themselves every thirty days
questions.explanation: The most distinctive thing about democracy is that its examination never gets over. As democracy passes one test, it produces another test. As people get some benefits of democracy, they ask for more and want to make democracy even better.

questions.question: A public that is vocal, critical, and continuously complains about government performance is considered:
options: A testimony to the success of democracy, showing citizens are alert and transform subjects into active participants
A sign of imminent civil collapse and institutional treason
A punishable offense under parliamentary penal codes
Proof that military dictatorship is immediately required
questions.explanation: A public expression of dissatisfaction with democracy shows the success of the democratic project: it transforms people from the status of a subject into that of a citizen. Most individuals today believe that their vote makes a difference.

questions.question: Surveys across South Asian nations (India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal) show that support for democracy is:
options: Restricted only to university professors and wealthy bankers
Non-existent, with over 90% preferring direct foreign rule
Widespread and overwhelmingly preferred over dictatorship across all countries
Declining rapidly in favor of military juntas in every country
questions.explanation: Evidence from South Asia shows that support for democracy exists across countries with democratic regimes as well as regimes without democracy. People wish to be ruled by representatives elected by them.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Civics, Chapter 5, Section 5.1 & Table on South Asia

questions.question: Why does a democracy provide better room to correct its own policy mistakes than an autocracy?
options: The Supreme Court automatically removes prime ministers every Sunday
Government policies are erased automatically after six months
All laws require unanimous consent of every adult citizen
Decisions are open to public debate and scrutiny, and ruling parties can be voted out if they refuse to rectify errors
questions.explanation: Democracy allows room to correct mistakes because mistakes cannot be hidden for long. There is a space for public discussion on these mistakes and room for correction; either rulers have to change their decisions or rulers themselves can be changed.

questions.question: What is the primary dilemma educators and political scientists observe when assessing democracy?
options: Democracy is practiced everywhere but has no written constitution
Democracy is seen as good in principle, but felt to be not so good in its actual practice
Democracy requires all citizens to serve in active combat forces
Democracy bans newspapers and independent investigative journalism
questions.explanation: Our fascination with democracy often pushes us into taking a position that democracy can address all socio-economic and political problems. We face a dilemma: democracy is seen to be good in principle, but felt to be not so good in its practice.
